safety.title: Safety
safety.disclaimer: Bato is not a rescue service and not medical advice. In an emergency, call the numbers below.
safety.testMode: TEST MODE: the emergency numbers below and the SOS fallback call the test numbers set in mobile/.env, not the real services.
safety.cardBody: Hold SOS to text your location to your contacts, even without mobile data.
safety.holdHint: Hold for 2 seconds to text your location to your emergency contacts
safety.holdA11y: SOS. Touch and hold for 2 seconds to send your location
safety.readyBody_one: Your messages app opened with your location for {{count}} contact. Press Send there.
safety.readyBody_other: Your messages app opened with your location for {{count}} contacts. Press Send there.
safety.notSentHint: If it didn't send, call the Tourist Police: {{phone}}.
safety.calledPolice: You have no emergency contacts, so Bato opened a call to the Tourist Police ({{phone}}).
safety.noLocation: No location: the message says so. Tell them where you are.
safety.failed: Could not open your messages. Call {{phone}} instead.
safety.contactsEmpty: No contacts yet. Add someone who should know if you are in trouble.
safety.contactsOffline: Kept on this phone too, so SOS works without internet.
safety.name: Name
safety.deleteBody: They will no longer get your SOS messages.
safety.maxContacts: You can save up to 5 contacts.
safety.nameAndPhone: Enter a name and a phone number.
safety.checkerIntro: Answer for how you feel right now. It is most useful after going higher, for example each evening on a trek.
safety.answer_headache_3: Severe headache, I can't do anything
safety.answer_gi_3: Severe nausea and vomiting, I can't do anything
safety.answer_fatigue_3: Severe tiredness or weakness, I can't do anything
safety.answer_dizziness_3: Severe dizziness, I can't do anything
safety.flagsHint: Tick any that are true. Any one of them means: go down now.
safety.flag_confusion: Confused, or can't walk in a straight line
safety.flag_breathless: Out of breath while resting, or a wet cough
safety.flag_worse_after_rest: Symptoms got worse after a rest day
safety.whereHint: Pick tonight's stop, or use the phone's GPS.
safety.gpsNone: The GPS gave no altitude. Pick a stop instead.
safety.resultBody_ok: Keep drinking water and go up slowly. Check again this evening, or sooner if you feel worse.
safety.resultBody_rest: Stay at this altitude until the symptoms are gone. If they get worse, go down.
safety.resultBody_descend: Go down now, at least 300 to 500 m, and not alone. Call for help.
safety.reason_LOW_SCORE: A score below 3: no sign of acute mountain sickness (AMS).
safety.reason_NO_HEADACHE: No headache, so this is not typical AMS, but your other symptoms are a reason to rest.
safety.reason_AMS_MILD: A headache and a score of 3 to 5: mild AMS.
safety.reason_AMS_MODERATE: A headache and a score of 6 to 9: moderate AMS.
safety.reason_AMS_SEVERE: A headache and a score of 10 to 12: severe AMS.
safety.reason_RED_FLAG_CONFUSION: Confusion or unsteady walking can be HACE (swelling of the brain).
safety.reason_RED_FLAG_BREATHLESS: Breathlessness at rest or a wet cough can be HAPE (fluid in the lungs).
safety.reason_RED_FLAG_WORSE_AFTER_REST: Symptoms that get worse after resting need a lower altitude.
safety.savedLater: Saved on this phone. It will be sent when you are online.
safety.source: Based on the 2018 Lake Louise AMS score (Roach et al., High Altitude Medicine & Biology).
safety.historyEmpty: No checks yet. Use "How do you feel?" on a trek.
